ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

content.content:
## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every **usable** root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction
----
## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations (O9–O11) do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is an active derived or root authority, and `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` holds; its origin chain and anchors are valid: every authority of its origin chain, its effective anchor included, is active.
2. The leaves of `region` exist and belong to the footprint of `source`; `mode` does not exceed the available effective right on these leaves.
3. The addition preserves exclusivity I1: no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible with the derived right, and already-active descendants are respected.
4. The new holding frame is the live current frame. The admissible state's footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true.

**`ok` effect:** A new active authority with fresh identity, origin `source`, requested mode and footprint, and held by the current frame is added. The source remains active; its effective modes are recomputed per leaf. No storage or place anchor is created. Multiple compatible observations remain permitted. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights

These transitions govern value consumption and the controlled movement of their dependencies. A valid transition can neither create an additional permission nor discard a surviving anchor.

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved. No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check. Authorities held by parts of `source` are transferred with the value and are controlled by §63.8.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
9. **Destination usability:** `destination` is usable in the resulting state.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor

**Preconditions**

1. `result` is a usable place over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
2. `anchor` designates an active, valid authority representing a real dependency of the relevant rights or storage; a declared dependency cannot extend an origin's lifetime.
3. Existing anchors are preserved and the addition respects `AnchorOrder`: the effective anchor's frame is the frame of `result` or an ancestor thereof.
4. Every dependency carried by a contained value remains represented in the transitive obligations of its container.

**`ok` effect:** `anchor` is added to `D(result)`; the container's transitive dependencies account for it. No additional access right is created. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

A safe interface must declare dependencies covering those actually required by its implementation; the annotation itself is not presumed true. An unsafe abstraction bears the obligations of its contract.

## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active, **derived**, and held by the current frame; a root authority can never be stored by `store`.
2. `target` is a usable **leaf** under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It holds no other **active** authority. Its data already being `Init` does not by itself prohibit the operation.
3. The stored authority covers neither a leaf of `target` nor the leaves of storage transitively owned by it.
4. The effective anchor of `authority` respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`; other dependencies are preserved.
5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.

**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.

# X. Reading, Writing, and Initialization

A leaf's initialization state and the effective right to access it are two distinct conditions.

## 66. O9 — Safe Reading of Regions

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf being read belongs to a usable place and is `Init`.
2. `access` is an authority exercisable in `Observe` mode over the region; its **effective** mode actually permits observation of each leaf being read.
3. Required anchors are valid, and the type and storage contract permits this read.

**`ok` effect:** The logical read succeeds, without modifying `F`, `P`, `I`, `A`, `D`, or arena entries. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

`Moved` and `Uninit` cannot be read. This definition does not replace concrete representation and pointer checks of the elementary memory machine.

## 67. O10 — Ordinary Write

**Preconditions**

1. Targeted leaves belong to usable places, and `access` is exercisable in `Modify` mode with **effective** `Modify` right over each leaf.
2. No incompatible ordinary authority holds an incompatible effective mode over the written leaves (I1).
3. Anchors and constraints of the relevant types, storage, and abstractions remain valid.

**`ok` effect:** The logical write sets the actually written leaves to `Init` and does not modify authorities or their anchors. An unwritten leaf does not become `Init` by this effect. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 68. O11 — Write Under Shared Mutation

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf in the region is usable and declared `K.SharedMutable`.
2. `access` is exercisable in a mode **at least** `Observe` and has a present effective mode on every leaf, either `Observe` or `Modify`; exercising an authority without an effective mode is insufficient.
3. Dependencies are valid and the particular shared-mutation discipline guaranteed by `K.SharedMutable` applies.

**`ok` effect:** Actually written leaves become `Init`; authorities and their structural exclusivity I1 do not change. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

`writeShared` may update metadata under an `Observe` authority when the contract permits. Stability of observed contents is not automatically guaranteed, and this kernel **does not prove** the absence of data races: that requires the concurrency model's guarantees.

246	/-- Conclusions of the iteration lie below the bound (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
247	theorem kiter_bound {n : Nat} {R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool} (h : KRule n R) :
248	    ∀ k a, kiter R k a = true → a < n
249	  | 0, _, hk => by simp [kiter] at hk
250	  | _ + 1, a, hk => h.bound _ a hk
251	
252	/-- `countP` is monotone in the predicate (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
253	theorem countP_le_of {l : List Nat} {p q : Nat → Bool} (hpq : ∀ a ∈ l, p a = true → q a = true) :
254	    l.countP p ≤ l.countP q := by
255	  induction l with
256	  | nil => simp
257	  | cons a l ih =>
258	    simp only [List.countP_cons]
259	    have := ih fun b hb => hpq b (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hb)
260	    cases hp : p a <;> cases hq : q a <;> simp_all <;> omega
261	
262	/-- `countP` grows strictly when one more element satisfies the predicate (decision procedure
263	for §40 and §43). -/
264	theorem countP_lt_of {l : List Nat} {p q : Nat → Bool} (hpq : ∀ a ∈ l, p a = true → q a = true)
265	    {x : Nat} (hx : x ∈ l) (hqx : q x = true) (hpx : p x = false) : l.countP p < l.countP q := by
266	  induction l with
267	  | nil => simp at hx
268	  | cons a l ih =>
269	    simp only [List.countP_cons]
270	    have hle := countP_le_of (l := l) fun b hb => hpq b (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hb)
271	    rcases List.mem_cons.1 hx with rfl | hx
272	    · simp [hqx, hpx]; omega
273	    · have := ih (fun b hb => hpq b (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hb)) hx
274	      cases hp : p a <;> cases hq : q a <;> simp_all <;> omega
275	
276	/-- A failed `all` has a witness (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
277	theorem all_false_exists {α : Type} {p : α → Bool} : ∀ {l : List α}, l.all p = false →
278	    ∃ a ∈ l, p a = false
279	  | [], h => by simp at h
280	  | a :: l, h => by
281	    simp only [List.all_cons, Bool.and_eq_false_iff] at h
282	    rcases h with h | h
283	    · exact ⟨a, List.mem_cons_self .., h⟩
284	    · obtain ⟨b, hb, hb'⟩ := all_false_exists h; exact ⟨b, List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hb, hb'⟩
285	
286	/-- Stability of the iteration at step `k`, below `n` (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
287	def kstab (R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool) (n k : Nat) : Bool :=
288	  (List.range n).all fun a => kiter R (k + 1) a == kiter R k a
289	
290	/-- A stable iteration stays stable one step later (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
291	theorem kstab_succ {n : Nat} {R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool} (h : KRule n R) {k : Nat}
292	    (hs : kstab R n k = true) : kstab R n (k + 1) = true := by
293	  simp only [kstab, List.all_eq_true, List.mem_range, beq_iff_eq] at hs ⊢
294	  intro a ha
295	  show R (kiter R (k + 1)) a = R (kiter R k) a
296	  exact h.loc _ _ (fun b hb => hs b hb) a
297	
298	/-- A stable iteration stays stable (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
299	theorem kstab_le {n : Nat} {R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool} (h : KRule n R) {k : Nat}
300	    (hs : kstab R n k = true) : ∀ j, k ≤ j → kstab R n j = true
301	  | j, hj => by
302	    induction j with
303	    | zero => obtain rfl : k = 0 := by omega
304	              exact hs
305	    | succ j ih =>
306	      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge k (j + 1) with hlt | hge
307	      · exact kstab_succ h (ih (by omega))
308	      · obtain rfl : k = j + 1 := by omega
309	        exact hs
310	
311	/-- Before stabilizing, each step adds a conclusion (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
312	theorem kstab_exists {n : Nat} {R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool} (h : KRule n R) :
313	    ∀ k, (∃ j, j < k ∧ kstab R n j = true) ∨ k ≤ (List.range n).countP (kiter R k)
314	  | 0 => .inr (Nat.zero_le _)
315	  | k + 1 => by
316	    rcases kstab_exists h k with hj | hc
317	    · obtain ⟨j, hj, hs⟩ := hj; exact .inl ⟨j, by omega, hs⟩
318	    · cases hs : kstab R n k
319	      · obtain ⟨a, ha, hne⟩ := all_false_exists hs
320	        simp only [List.mem_range, beq_eq_false_iff_ne] at ha hne
321	        have hk : kiter R k a = false := by
322	          cases e : kiter R k a
323	          · rfl
324	          · exact absurd (kiter_mono h k a e) (by rw [e] at hne; simpa using hne)
325	        have hk1 : kiter R (k + 1) a = true := by
326	          cases e : kiter R (k + 1) a
327	          · rw [e, hk] at hne; exact absurd rfl hne
328	          · rfl
329	        have := countP_lt_of (l := List.range n) (fun b _ hb => kiter_mono h k b hb)
330	          (List.mem_range.2 ha) hk1 hk
331	        exact .inr (by omega)
332	      · exact .inl ⟨k, by omega, hs⟩
333	
334	/-- The iteration is stable from step `n + 1` on (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
335	theorem kiter_fix {n : Nat} {R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool} (h : KRule n R) (a : Nat) :
336	    kiter R (n + 2) a = kiter R (n + 1) a := by
337	  rcases kstab_exists h (n + 1) with ⟨j, hj, hs⟩ | hc
338	  · have hs' := kstab_le h hs (n + 1) (by omega)
339	    by_cases ha : a < n
340	    · simp only [kstab, List.all_eq_true, List.mem_range, beq_iff_eq] at hs'
341	      exact hs' a ha
342	    · cases e : kiter R (n + 2) a
343	      · cases e' : kiter R (n + 1) a
344	        · rfl
345	        · exact absurd (kiter_bound h _ a e') ha
346	      · exact absurd (kiter_bound h _ a e) ha
347	  · have := List.countP_le_length (p := kiter R (n + 1)) (l := List.range n)
348	    simp at this; omega
349	
350	/-- Monotonicity of the iteration over several steps (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
351	theorem kiter_mono_le {n : Nat} {R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool} (h : KRule n R) :
352	    ∀ j k a, kiter R k a = true → kiter R (k + j) a = true
353	  | 0, _, _, hk => hk
354	  | j + 1, k, a, hk => kiter_mono h _ a (kiter_mono_le h j k a hk)
355	
356	/-- The iteration is constant after step `n + 1` (decision procedure for §40 and §43). -/
357	theorem kiter_ge {n : Nat} {R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool} (h : KRule n R) :
358	    ∀ j, kiter R (n + 1 + j) = kiter R (n + 1)
359	  | 0 => rfl
360	  | j + 1 => funext fun a => by
361	    show R (kiter R (n + 1 + j)) a = kiter R (n + 1) a
362	    rw [kiter_ge h j]; exact kiter_fix h a
363	
364	/-- A conclusion reached at some step is reached at step `n + 1` (decision procedure for §40 and
365	§43). -/
366	theorem kiter_up {n : Nat} {R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool} (h : KRule n R) :
367	    ∀ k a, kiter R k a = true → kiter R (n + 1) a = true := by
368	  intro k a hk
369	  by_cases hkn : k ≤ n + 1
370	  · have := kiter_mono_le h (n + 1 - k) k a hk
371	    rwa [show k + (n + 1 - k) = n + 1 by omega] at this
372	  · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ : ∃ j, k = n + 1 + j := ⟨k - (n + 1), by omega⟩
373	    rwa [kiter_ge h j] at hk

375	/-! ## Usable places (§40) -/
376	
377	/-- `Usable(s, p)` (§40, items 1–3): `p` exists, is not marked dead, and its owner is a frame of
378	the stack or a usable place. Inductive, so an ownership cycle makes no place usable (§40). -/
379	inductive S3.Usable (s : S3) : Nat → Prop where
380	  | frame {q f : Nat} {pl : Place} : s.P[q]? = some pl → s.dead q = false →
381	      pl.owner = .frame f → f ∈ s.F → S3.Usable s q
382	  | place {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} : s.P[q]? = some pl → s.dead q = false →
383	      pl.owner = .place o → S3.Usable s o → S3.Usable s q
384	
385	/-- A usable place exists (§40, item 1). -/
386	theorem S3.Usable.lt {s : S3} {q : Nat} (h : s.Usable q) : q < s.P.length := by
387	  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
388	
389	/-- One step of `Usable` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §40). -/
390	def usableR (s : S3) (U : Nat → Bool) (q : Nat) : Bool :=
391	  match s.P[q]? with
392	  | some pl => !s.dead q && match pl.owner with
393	    | .frame f => decide (f ∈ s.F)
394	    | .place o => decide (o < s.P.length) && U o
395	  | none => false
396	
397	/-- The place case of `usableR` (decision procedure for §40). -/
398	theorem usableR_place {s : S3} {U : Nat → Bool} {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} (hpl : s.P[q]? = some pl)
399	    (hd : s.dead q = false) (ho : pl.owner = .place o) (hlt : o < s.P.length) (hU : U o = true) :
400	    usableR s U q = true := by
401	  simp [usableR, hpl, hd, ho, hlt, hU]
402	
403	/-- `usableR` is a bounded monotone rule (decision procedure for §40). -/
404	theorem usableR_rule (s : S3) : KRule s.P.length (usableR s) where
405	  mono p q hpq a h := by
406	    unfold usableR at h ⊢; split at h
407	    · split at h <;> simp_all
408	    · exact h
409	  bound p a h := by
410	    unfold usableR at h; split at h
411	    · exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
412	    · cases h
413	  loc p q hpq a := by
414	    unfold usableR; split
415	    · split
416	      · rfl
417	      · rename_i o _; by_cases ho : o < s.P.length <;> simp [ho, hpq o]
418	    · rfl
419	
420	/-- Soundness of the iteration for `Usable` (decision procedure for §40). -/
421	theorem usable_of_kiter (s : S3) : ∀ k q, kiter (usableR s) k q = true → s.Usable q
422	  | 0, _, h => by simp [kiter] at h
423	  | k + 1, q, h => by
424	    simp only [kiter, usableR] at h
425	    split at h
426	    · rename_i pl hpl
427	      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.not_eq_true'] at h
428	      obtain ⟨hd, h⟩ := h
429	      split at h
430	      · exact .frame hpl hd ‹_› (by simpa using h)
431	      · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
432	        exact .place hpl hd ‹_› (usable_of_kiter s k _ h.2)
433	    · cases h
434	
435	/-- `Usable` is computed by `|P| + 1` steps of `usableR` (decision procedure for §40). -/
436	theorem usable_iff {s : S3} {q : Nat} :
437	    s.Usable q ↔ kiter (usableR s) (s.P.length + 1) q = true := by
438	  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, usable_of_kiter s _ q⟩
439	  induction h with
440	  | frame hpl hd ho hf =>
441	    show usableR s _ _ = true
442	    simp [usableR, hpl, hd, ho, hf]
443	  | place hpl hd ho hu ih =>
444	    rw [← kiter_fix (usableR_rule s)]
445	    show usableR s _ _ = true
446	    exact usableR_place hpl hd ho hu.lt ih
447	
448	/-- Decidability of `Usable` (§40). -/
449	instance (s : S3) (q : Nat) : Decidable (s.Usable q) := decidable_of_iff _ usable_iff.symm
450	
451	/-- Live holder (§49.8): a frame of the stack or a usable place. -/
452	def HolderLive (s : S3) : Holder → Prop
453	  | .frame f => f ∈ s.F
454	  | .place p => s.Usable p
455	
456	/-- Decidability of `HolderLive` (§49.8). -/
457	instance (s : S3) (h : Holder) : Decidable (HolderLive s h) := by
458	  cases h <;> unfold HolderLive <;> infer_instance

460	/-! ## Frame of a place (§40, §44) -/
461	
462	/-- Frame ending the ownership chain of `q`, searched within `k` steps (`placeFrame`, §40). -/
463	def pframeF (s : S3) : Nat → Nat → Option Nat
464	  | 0, _ => none
465	  | k + 1, q =>
466	    match s.P[q]? with
467	    | some pl =>
468	      match pl.owner with
469	      | .frame f => some f
470	      | .place o => pframeF s k o
471	    | none => none
472	
473	/-- `placeFrame(q)` (§40): the frame ending the ownership chain of `q`, within `|P| + 1`
474	steps. -/
475	def S3.pframe (s : S3) (q : Nat) : Option Nat := pframeF s (s.P.length + 1) q
476	
477	/-- Frame of a holder (§44): the frame itself, or the frame of the holding place. -/
478	def S3.hframe (s : S3) : Holder → Option Nat
479	  | .frame f => some f
480	  | .place p => s.pframe p
481	
482	/-- `FrameOf s q f` (§40, `placeFrame`; §49.3): the ownership chain of `q` is finite and ends at
483	frame `f`. -/
484	inductive FrameOf (s : S3) : Nat → Nat → Prop where
485	  | frame {q f : Nat} {pl : Place} : s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f → FrameOf s q f
486	  | place {q o f : Nat} {pl : Place} : s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o → FrameOf s o f →
487	      FrameOf s q f
488	
489	/-- A place with a frame exists (§40). -/
490	theorem FrameOf.lt {s : S3} {q f : Nat} (h : FrameOf s q f) : q < s.P.length := by
491	  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
492	
493	/-- One step of `FrameOf s · f` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §40). -/
494	def frR (s : S3) (f : Nat) (U : Nat → Bool) (q : Nat) : Bool :=
495	  match s.P[q]? with
496	  | some pl => match pl.owner with
497	    | .frame g => decide (g = f)
498	    | .place o => decide (o < s.P.length) && U o
499	  | none => false
500	
501	/-- `frR` is a bounded monotone rule (decision procedure for §40). -/
502	theorem frR_rule (s : S3) (f : Nat) : KRule s.P.length (frR s f) where
503	  mono p q hpq a h := by
504	    unfold frR at h ⊢; split at h
505	    · split at h <;> simp_all
506	    · exact h
507	  bound p a h := by
508	    unfold frR at h; split at h
509	    · exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
510	    · cases h
511	  loc p q hpq a := by
512	    unfold frR; split
513	    · split
514	      · rfl
515	      · rename_i o _; by_cases ho : o < s.P.length <;> simp [ho, hpq o]
516	    · rfl
517	
518	/-- `pframeF` is the iteration of `frR` (decision procedure for §40). -/
519	theorem pframeF_kiter (s : S3) (f : Nat) :
520	    ∀ k q, pframeF s k q = some f ↔ kiter (frR s f) k q = true
521	  | 0, q => by simp [pframeF, kiter]
522	  | k + 1, q => by
523	    simp only [pframeF, kiter, frR]
524	    split
525	    · split
526	      · simp
527	      · rename_i o _
528	        by_cases hlt : o < s.P.length
529	        · simp [hlt, pframeF_kiter s f k o]
530	        · simp only [hlt, decide_false, Bool.false_and]
531	          cases k with
532	          | zero => simp [pframeF]
533	          | succ k => simp [pframeF, List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 (Nat.le_of_not_lt hlt)]
534	    · simp
535	
536	/-- Soundness of the iteration for `FrameOf` (decision procedure for §40). -/
537	theorem frameOf_of_kiter (s : S3) (f : Nat) : ∀ k q, kiter (frR s f) k q = true → FrameOf s q f
538	  | 0, _, h => by simp [kiter] at h
539	  | k + 1, q, h => by
540	    simp only [kiter, frR] at h
541	    split at h
542	    · rename_i pl hpl
543	      split at h
544	      · rename_i g hg; simp only [decide_eq_true_eq] at h; subst h; exact .frame hpl hg
545	      · rename_i o ho; simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
546	        exact .place hpl ho (frameOf_of_kiter s f k o h.2)
547	    · cases h
548	
549	/-- `pframe` computes `FrameOf` (§40, `placeFrame`). -/
550	theorem pframe_iff {s : S3} {q f : Nat} : s.pframe q = some f ↔ FrameOf s q f := by
551	  rw [S3.pframe, pframeF_kiter]
552	  refine ⟨frameOf_of_kiter s f _ q, fun h => ?_⟩
553	  induction h with
554	  | frame hpl ho => exact kiter_up (frR_rule s _) 1 _ (by simp [kiter, frR, hpl, ho])
555	  | place hpl ho hf ih =>
556	    apply kiter_up (frR_rule s _) (s.P.length + 2) _
557	    show frR s _ (kiter (frR s _) (s.P.length + 1)) _ = true
558	    simp [frR, hpl, ho, ih, hf.lt]

561	
562	/-- One step of `OwnedIn P src` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §40). -/
563	def owR (P : List Place) (src : Nat) (U : Nat → Bool) (q : Nat) : Bool :=
564	  match P[q]? with
565	  | some pl => match pl.owner with
566	    | .place o => decide (partOf P o src) || (decide (o < P.length) && U o)
567	    | .frame _ => false
568	  | none => false

570	/-- A place owned through the value at `src` exists (§40). -/
571	theorem OwnedIn.lt {P : List Place} {src q : Nat} (h : OwnedIn P src q) : q < P.length := by
572	  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
573	
574	/-- `owR` is a bounded monotone rule (decision procedure for §40). -/
575	theorem owR_rule (P : List Place) (src : Nat) : KRule P.length (owR P src) where
576	  mono p q hpq a h := by
577	    unfold owR at h ⊢; split at h
578	    · split at h
579	      · simp only [Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h ⊢
580	        rcases h with h | ⟨h1, h2⟩
581	        · exact .inl h
582	        · exact .inr ⟨h1, hpq _ h2⟩
583	      · exact h
584	    · exact h
585	  bound p a h := by
586	    unfold owR at h; split at h
587	    · exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
588	    · cases h
589	  loc p q hpq a := by
590	    unfold owR; split
591	    · split
592	      · rename_i o _; by_cases ho : o < P.length <;> simp [ho, hpq o]
593	      · rfl
594	    · rfl

596	/-- Soundness of the iteration for `OwnedIn` (decision procedure for §40). -/
597	theorem ownedIn_of_kiter (P : List Place) (src : Nat) :
598	    ∀ k q, kiter (owR P src) k q = true → OwnedIn P src q
599	  | 0, _, h => by simp [kiter] at h
600	  | k + 1, q, h => by
601	    simp only [kiter, owR] at h
602	    split at h
603	    · rename_i pl hpl
604	      split at h
605	      · rename_i o ho
606	        simp only [Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
607	        rcases h with h | ⟨-, h⟩
608	        · exact .direct hpl ho h
609	        · exact .step hpl ho (ownedIn_of_kiter P src k o h)
610	      · cases h
611	    · cases h

613	/-- `OwnedIn` is computed by `|P| + 1` steps of `owR` (decision procedure for §40). -/
614	theorem ownedIn_iff {P : List Place} {src q : Nat} :
615	    OwnedIn P src q ↔ kiter (owR P src) (P.length + 1) q = true := by
616	  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, ownedIn_of_kiter P src _ q⟩
617	  induction h with
618	  | direct hpl ho hp => exact kiter_up (owR_rule P src) 1 _ (by simp [kiter, owR, hpl, ho, hp])
619	  | step hpl ho ho' ih =>
620	    apply kiter_up (owR_rule P src) (P.length + 2) _
621	    show owR P src (kiter (owR P src) (P.length + 1)) _ = true
622	    simp [owR, hpl, ho, ih, ho'.lt]

624	/-- Decidability of `OwnedIn` (§40). -/
625	instance (P : List Place) (src q : Nat) : Decidable (OwnedIn P src q) :=
626	  decidable_of_iff _ ownedIn_iff.symm

628	/-! ## Effective modes (§43) -/
629	
630	/-- Modes of the active descendants of `a` whose footprint covers leaf `p` (§43). -/
631	def descModes (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : List Mode :=
632	  (List.range s.A.length).filterMap fun j =>
633	    match s.A[j]? with
634	    | some y => if y.active = true ∧ p ∈ y.footprint ∧ a ∈ s.ancs j then some y.mode else none
635	    | none => none
636	
637	/-- Cases 2–4 of §43 for an active authority of own mode `m` covering the leaf, whose covering
638	active descendants have modes `ds`. -/
639	def effOf (m : Mode) (ds : List Mode) : Option Mode :=
640	  if ds = [] then some m else if Mode.modify ∈ ds then none else some .observe
641	
642	/-- `effective(s, a, l)` (§43, cases 1–4), computed per leaf. -/
643	def effective (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Option Mode :=
644	  match s.A[a]? with
645	  | some x => if x.active = true ∧ p ∈ x.footprint then effOf x.mode (descModes s a p) else none
646	  | none => none
647	
648	/-- Compatible effective modes for independent ordinary accesses: only `Observe`/`Observe`
649	(§50). -/
650	def Compat (m₁ m₂ : Mode) : Prop := m₁ = .observe ∧ m₂ = .observe
651	
652	/-- Effective mode `e` permits the requested mode `m`: present and not exceeded (§43). -/
653	def Allows (e : Option Mode) (m : Mode) : Prop := OptP e (fun e => m.le e) False
654	
655	/-- Decidability of `Allows` (§43). -/
656	instance (e : Option Mode) (m : Mode) : Decidable (Allows e m) := by
657	  unfold Allows; infer_instance
658	
659	/-- Footprint of authority `a` (§42), empty if it does not exist. -/
660	def S3.afp (s : S3) (a : Nat) : List Nat := match s.A[a]? with
661	  | some x => x.footprint
662	  | none => []
663	
664	/-- Adds an authority with fresh identity `s.A.length` (§42, §60). -/
665	def S3.addAuth (s : S3) (y : Authority) : S3 := { s with A := s.A ++ [y] }
666	
667	/-! ## Exercisable authorities (§43) -/
668	
669	/-- `ExercisableAt(s, a, m)` (§43): `a` is active, its own mode permits `m`, and it is held by
670	the current frame, or by a place `p` such that an authority itself exercisable at `m` has an
671	effective mode permitting `m` on every leaf of `p`. Inductive along the holder chain (§43), so no
672	holder cycle justifies a right. -/
673	inductive S3.ExercisableAt (s : S3) : Nat → Mode → Prop where
674	  | base {a : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true → m.le y.mode →
675	      y.holder = .frame s.top → S3.ExercisableAt s a m
676	  | held {a p b : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true →
677	      m.le y.mode → y.holder = .place p → S3.ExercisableAt s b m →
678	      (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m) → S3.ExercisableAt s a m
679	
680	/-- One step of `ExercisableAt · m` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §43). -/
681	def exR (s : S3) (m : Mode) (E : Nat → Bool) (a : Nat) : Bool :=
682	  match s.A[a]? with
683	  | some y => y.active && decide (m.le y.mode) && match y.holder with
684	    | .frame f => decide (f = s.top)
685	    | .place p => (List.range s.A.length).any fun b =>
686	        decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m) && E b
687	  | none => false
688	
689	/-- `any` depends only on the values of the predicate on the list (decision procedure for
690	§43). -/
691	theorem any_congr' {α : Type} {f g : α → Bool} : ∀ {l : List α}, (∀ b ∈ l, f b = g b) →
692	    l.any f = l.any g
693	  | [], _ => rfl
694	  | a :: l, h => by
695	    simp only [List.any_cons, h a (List.mem_cons_self ..),
696	      any_congr' fun b hb => h b (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hb)]
697	
698	/-- `exR` is a bounded monotone rule (decision procedure for §43). -/
699	theorem exR_rule (s : S3) (m : Mode) : KRule s.A.length (exR s m) where
700	  mono p q hpq a h := by
701	    unfold exR at h ⊢; split at h
702	    · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h ⊢
703	      refine ⟨h.1, ?_⟩; split at h
704	      · simpa using h.2
705	      · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, List.any_eq_true] at h ⊢
706	        obtain ⟨b, hb, hc, he⟩ := h.2
707	        exact ⟨b, hb, hc, hpq b he⟩
708	    · exact h
709	  bound p a h := by
710	    unfold exR at h; split at h
711	    · exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
712	    · cases h
713	  loc p q hpq a := by
714	    unfold exR; split
715	    · congr 1; split
716	      · rfl
717	      · exact any_congr' fun b hb => by rw [hpq b (List.mem_range.1 hb)]
718	    · rfl
719	
720	/-- Soundness of the iteration for `ExercisableAt` (decision procedure for §43). -/
721	theorem exercisableAt_of_kiter (s : S3) (m : Mode) :
722	    ∀ k a, kiter (exR s m) k a = true → s.ExercisableAt a m
723	  | 0, _, h => by simp [kiter] at h
724	  | k + 1, a, h => by
725	    simp only [kiter, exR] at h
726	    split at h
727	    · rename_i y hy
728	      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
729	      obtain ⟨⟨ha, hm⟩, h⟩ := h
730	      split at h
731	      · rename_i f hf; exact .base hy ha hm (by simp at h; rw [hf, h])
732	      · rename_i p hp
733	        simp only [List.any_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
734	        obtain ⟨b, -, hc, hb⟩ := h
735	        exact .held hy ha hm hp (exercisableAt_of_kiter s m k b hb) hc
736	    · cases h
737	
738	/-- The frame-held case of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
739	theorem exR_base {s : S3} {m : Mode} {E : Nat → Bool} {a : Nat} {y : Authority}
740	    (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (ha : y.active = true) (hm : m.le y.mode)
741	    (hf : y.holder = .frame s.top) : exR s m E a = true := by
742	  unfold exR; rw [hy]; simp [ha, hm, hf]
743	
744	/-- The place-held case of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
745	theorem exR_held {s : S3} {m : Mode} {E : Nat → Bool} {a p b : Nat} {y : Authority}
746	    (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (ha : y.active = true) (hm : m.le y.mode) (hp : y.holder = .place p)
747	    (hb : b < s.A.length) (hc : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m)
748	    (hE : E b = true) : exR s m E a = true := by
749	  simp only [exR, hy, ha, hp, Bool.true_and, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq,
750	    List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
751	  exact ⟨hm, b, hb, hc, hE⟩
752	
753	/-- `ExercisableAt` is computed by `|A| + 1` steps of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
754	theorem exercisableAt_iff {s : S3} {a : Nat} {m : Mode} :
755	    s.ExercisableAt a m ↔ kiter (exR s m) (s.A.length + 1) a = true := by
756	  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, exercisableAt_of_kiter s m _ a⟩
757	  induction h with
758	  | base hy ha hm hf => exact exR_base hy ha hm hf
759	  | held hy ha hm hp hb hc ih =>
760	    rw [← kiter_fix (exR_rule s _)]
761	    have hb' := kiter_bound (exR_rule s _) _ _ ih
762	    exact exR_held hy ha hm hp hb' hc ih
763	
764	/-- Decidability of `ExercisableAt` (§43). -/
765	instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (m : Mode) : Decidable (s.ExercisableAt a m) :=
766	  decidable_of_iff _ exercisableAt_iff.symm
767	
768	/-- `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43): the current frame has an authority exercisable at `m` whose
769	effective mode permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
770	def HasRight (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
771	  ∃ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.ExercisableAt a m ∧
772	    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s a l) m
773	
774	/-- Decidability of `HasRight` (§43). -/
775	instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Decidable (HasRight s m q) := by
776	  unfold HasRight; infer_instance
777	
778	/-- Authority `g` grounds the right `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43; §63.4, §69.2, §70.3: "the
779	exercisable authority on which that right rests"): it is exercisable at `m` and its effective mode
780	permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
781	def Grounds (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Prop :=
782	  g ∈ List.range s.A.length ∧ s.ExercisableAt g m ∧
783	    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s g l) m
784	
785	/-- Decidability of `Grounds` (§63.4, §69.2, §70.3). -/
786	instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Decidable (Grounds s m q g) := by
787	  unfold Grounds; infer_instance
788	
789	/-- Authority `j` is the grounding authority `g` or belongs to its origin chain (§63.4, §69.2,
790	§70.3: "the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain"). -/
791	def RightChain (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Prop := j = g ∨ j ∈ s.ancs g
792	
793	/-- Decidability of `RightChain` (§63.4, §69.2, §70.3). -/
794	instance (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Decidable (RightChain s g j) := by
795	  unfold RightChain; infer_instance

797	/-! ## Dependencies and anchors (§44) -/
798	
799	/-- Anchors of the value at `q`, inherited from its parts (§44: dependencies of contained values
800	are accounted for transitively). -/
801	def depsOf (s : S3) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
802	  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun r => decide (partOf s.P r q)).flatMap s.D
803	
804	/-- The anchors of every place containing leaf `p` are valid, that is, active (§44; §66.3,
805	§67.3, §68.3). -/
806	def DepsValid (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
807	  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, partOf s.P p q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x
808	
809	/-- Decidability of `DepsValid` (§44). -/
810	instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (DepsValid s p) :=
811	  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _ ∈ _, _))
812	
813	/-- The frame of the effective anchor of `x` (the frame of its holder) exists and is `fd` or an
814	ancestor of `fd` (§44). -/
815	def EffAnchorOK (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Prop :=
816	  OptP (s.A[s.effAnchor x]?) (fun z => OptP (s.hframe z.holder)
817	    (fun g => OptP fd (fun f => ancestor s.F g f) False) False) False
818	
819	/-- Decidability of `EffAnchorOK` (§44). -/
820	instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Decidable (EffAnchorOK s x fd) := by
821	  unfold EffAnchorOK; infer_instance
822	
823	/-- `AnchorOrder` (§44, §54): for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, the frame of the
824	effective anchor of `x` is the frame of `q` or an ancestor. -/
825	def AnchorOrder (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)
826	
827	/-- `AnchorOrder` read on the places of `P` (decision procedure for §44). -/
828	theorem anchorOrder_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrder s ↔
829	    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q) :=
830	  ⟨fun h q _ hq => h q hq, fun h q hq => h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq⟩
831	
832	/-- Decidability of `AnchorOrder` (§44). -/
833	instance (s : S3) : Decidable (AnchorOrder s) := decidable_of_iff _ anchorOrder_iff.symm
834	
835	/-- `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54): the rule of `AnchorOrder` for every active authority held by a
836	usable place `q`. -/
837	def AnchorOrderHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
838	  ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
839	    y.holder = .place q → EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)
840	
841	/-- `AnchorOrderHeld` read on the places of `P` and the authorities of `A` (decision procedure for
842	§44). -/
843	theorem anchorOrderHeld_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrderHeld s ↔
844	    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length,
845	      OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
846	        EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)) True := by
847	  constructor
848	  · intro h q _ hq x _
849	    unfold OptP; split
850	    · rename_i y hy; exact h q hq x y hy
851	    · trivial
852	  · intro h q hq x y hy ya hh
853	    have := h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy))
854	    simp only [OptP, hy] at this; exact this ya hh
855	
856	/-- Decidability of `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44). -/
857	instance (s : S3) : Decidable (AnchorOrderHeld s) := decidable_of_iff _ anchorOrderHeld_iff.symm
858	
859	/-! ## Outcomes (§58) -/
860	
861	/-- `Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail` (§58). `fail` leaves the state unchanged and
862	carries none. -/
863	inductive Outcome3 (σ : Type) where
864	  | ok (s : σ)
865	  | reject
866	  | fail
867	
868	/-- A kernel transition other than `alloc` (§58): `ok` with the effect when the preconditions
869	hold, `reject` otherwise; never `fail`. -/
870	inductive Guarded {σ : Type} (Pre : Prop) (eff : σ) : Outcome3 σ → Prop where
871	  | ok : Pre → Guarded Pre eff (.ok eff)
872	  | reject : ¬ Pre → Guarded Pre eff .reject
873

1011:  | transfer {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat} : TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
1016:  | read {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} : Read3Step a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
1017:  | write {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} : Write3Step a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
